newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE COME FROM BEHIND, HOLD WORLD CHAMPIONS 1-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE COME FROM BEHIND, HOLD WORLD CHAMPIONS 1-1.

text.p: A 60th-minute equaliser by substitute striker Marc Keller gave 1998 World Cup hosts France a 1-1 draw with world champions Brazil in the opening match of the four-team Tournoi de France on Tuesday.
Real Madrid's Roberto Carlos put a wicked bend on the ball in typical Brazilian fashion to give Mario Zagallo's team the lead in spectacular fashion in the 21st minute.

His left-footed free kick, just to the right of centre and about 35 metres out, curled round France's four-man wall and in off Fabien Barthez's left-hand post with the surprised Monaco goalkeeper rooted to the spot.
France equalised in a move started by tricky right-sided midfielder Ibrahim Ba, who fed striker Florian Maurice, playing on the ground of his club Lyon.
Maurice's low shot was blocked by the diving Taffarel. But Karlsruhe's Keller, who came on for Robert Pires after the interval, pounced on the loose ball to nudge it into the net.
England and Italy, rivals in the same World Cup qualifying group, meet in the second match of the tournament, a dress rehearsal for next year's World Cup finals, in Nantes on Wednesday.
Zagallo, using a well worn cliche, said: "It was a match of two halves.
"I liked what the (Brazilian) selection did in the first half... France were better than Brazil in the second half."
Zagallo said he was satisfied given that Brazil rarely have time to train when they get together for matches.
"One year from the World Cup finals, Brazil can't be at their top," the veteran coach said.

Brazil, in the words of France coach Aime Jacquet "vexed by their defeat in Oslo (4-2 to Norway on Friday), full of conviction, concentration, aggression", forced the French on to their heels in the first half.

Strike pair Ronaldo and Romario were full of good runs that pierced the French defence. Barthez tipped over a fierce drive from the Barcelona player, set up with a fine cross ball by Flamengo's World Cup veteran, early on.
At the other end a minute later Taffarel saved from Ba at the feet of the AC Milan-bound Bordeaux player after he was put through by Zinedine Zidane.

Barthez also had to push over a hard shot from Brazil's right back Cafu, while Taffarel showed that even Brazilian goalkeepers have ball skills as he dangerously juggled with a back pass inside the six-yard box before clearing with a kick.
A free kick on the edge of the six-yard box four minutes into the second half presaged France's equaliser.
The whole Brazilian team stood on the goal-line but there was a metre wide gap to Taffarel's right where Zidane aimed his shot from the tapped free kick only for it to rebound off Cafu's leg.

Brazil captain Dunga brought a save from Barthez with a drive from outside the box and central defender Celio Silva was just wide with his header from the resulting corner as Brazil were forced deeper and attacked on the break.
France created numerous chances, one of the best in the dying minutes on the left where Athletic Bilbao left back Bixente Lizarazu and Keller set up Zidane, whose shot was just wide of the far post.
Jacquet said: "The French team showed a very reassuring face, especially in the second half, against a very difficult team.
"We managed to handle well the tough defensive work they put us through."

Sampdoria's Christian Karembeu, injured early on and substituted in the France team by Arsenal midfielder Patrick Vieira, went to hospital for an Xray. The French team said he might have a serious ankle injury.
